newsitem.title: DUBAI: Qatar says disagreement with Bahrain unresolved.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says disagreement with Bahrain unresolved.

text.p: Qatar and Bahrain still disagree on how to ease tensions over their territorial dispute and "distant positions" have delayed the signing of a Gulf-mediated deal, Qatar's foreign minister said on Monday.

Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said both countries had objected to different points in the seven-point document, forged by a committee of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
He did not elaborate, but hinted that the document touched on the territorial dispute, which he said it was not mandated to do by a Gulf Arab summit which formed the committee in December.
His comments were carried by the official Qatar News Agency.
The Qatari foreign minister stressed that the memorandum was only meant to defuse the war of words between the two countries, paving the way for efforts to settle the dispute.
"We did not reject everything and we did not accept everything. And likewise, our Bahraini brothers did not reject everything and did not accept everything," he said.
He said Qatar had asked for an explanation of some points that were unclear.
He said "distant positions" between Doha and Manama was one reason preventing the signing of the document, but hoped "that a brotherly solution will be reached".
The committee met in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Sunday night and the Qatari and Bahraini foreign ministers were expected to sign the document.

Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency said the mediation committee would visit Qatar and Bahrain soon to continue its efforts. It said Manama had welcomed the memorandum but added Qatar submitted a new proposal to the mediation committee on Sunday. It did not provide details.
Qatar took the territorial dispute to the International Court of Justice at the Hague in 1991, a move opposed by Bahrain.
Ties were further strained after Bahrain accused two Qataris of spying -- which Qatar denied -- and boycotted the Gulf Cooperation Council's December summit in Doha. Bahrain pardoned the two Qataris.
